readings: Matching lab tests to patients, average the CPK-to-GPT ratio for each `SEX` value, ignoring tests where the ratio is missing. Keep the sexes whose average is above the mean of those averages, then among them keep the ones above their own mean. In one unrounded row, give the average ratio of the sexes left, how far above the first mean they are on average, and how far above the second mean they are on average.
queries:
WITH sex_averages AS (
    SELECT p.SEX, AVG(1.0 * l.CPK / NULLIF(l.GPT, 0)) AS avg_ratio
    FROM Patient AS p
    JOIN Laboratory AS l ON l.ID = p.ID
    GROUP BY p.SEX
),
first_mean AS (
    SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) AS value FROM sex_averages
),
first_selected AS (
    SELECT s.avg_ratio
    FROM sex_averages AS s
    CROSS JOIN first_mean AS m
    WHERE s.avg_ratio > m.value
),
second_mean AS (
    SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) AS value FROM first_selected
)
SELECT
    AVG(s.avg_ratio) AS average_ratio,
    AVG(s.avg_ratio - f.value) AS above_first_mean,
    AVG(s.avg_ratio - m.value) AS above_second_mean
FROM first_selected AS s
CROSS JOIN first_mean AS f
CROSS JOIN second_mean AS m
WHERE s.avg_ratio > m.value
